title: Cycle Identity Preimage (patternlike.cycle-id.v1)
description: Closed preimage for cyc_ ids. Private to the calculation service and the trusted plane: oriented_branch and winding never appear on the wire or in a clear column, because they are what makes the id reproducible rather than what a client needs. Pass timestamps are deliberately absent — complete discovery may refine them, while the epoch-anchored (branch, winding) pair names the same physical encounter across shifted scan horizons. That is what lets two overlapping request windows return one identical cycle instead of two.

orientedBranch.description: Which oriented target longitude this encounter crosses. targets(N, A) = unique(norm360(N + A), norm360(N - A)); conjunction and opposition collapse to one target ('single') and every aspect strictly between 0 and 180 has two distinct branches.

target.description: The natal target: a celestial body id, or an angle id when angles are available.

winding.description: Integer lift k for the unwrapped target T = T0 + 360k, measured from the policy's fixed unwrapping_epoch. A later full revolution crosses the next winding and is a new cycle, so a body returning to the same aspect years later does not collide with its earlier encounter.

cycle_policy_version.description: Must bump whenever the ephemeris or container, the unwrapping epoch or its checkpoints, the scan grid, the station and root tolerances, or the complete-encounter lookaround can alter output. The persisted cycle_instances.horizon_version records this same value, so a threshold change re-scans into a new vintage instead of mixing vintages in one table.
